papers.summary: Spectral weight decay applies additive singular-value shrinkage. At 500M parameters and a 4% validation-loss distortion budget, it reports 1.89× SVD-LLM compression and 1.18× GPU inference speedup, versus 1.14× and 1.01× after standard weight decay.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses training for low-rank compressibility, spectral regularization, and label-noise robustness.

evidence.quote: For the 500 500 M model and a 4 % 4\% distortion budget, it supports 1.89 × 1.89\times compression, compared with 1.14 × 1.14\times after standard weight decay.
The factorized models outperform their dense counterparts only at large batch sizes, so we measure forward-pass latency with a batch size of 256 256 on a single GPU.

papers.title: Spectral Weight Decay: Inducing Low-Rank Structure in Neural Network Weights

papers.summary: Ori tracks drifting low-rank gradient subspaces during LLM pretraining. For 1B LLaMA at rank 32, the reported optimizer-step peak memory is 0.2487 GB versus 0.3385 GB for GaLore, with average step times of 12.6705 and 13.0401 seconds.
papers.relevance: A close fit for low-rank gradients and pretraining quality, optimizer memory, and time tradeoffs.

evidence.quote: We report validation perplexity after a fixed token budget, with full details provided in Appendix E .
For instance, at rank 32, Ori requires only 0.2487 GB, which is 12.1% less than OSD (0.2832 GB) and 26.5% less than GaLore (0.3385 GB).

papers.title: Ori: Drift-Aware Streaming $k$-PCA for Very Low-Rank LLM Training

papers.summary: Module-matched rank sweeps test LoRA against dense fine-tuning under label noise. In Qwen2.5-7B, the authors report that the post-peak LoRA gap to dense remains positive at every measured rank.
papers.relevance: Connects adapter rank, parameter savings, and generalization under noisy labels to a dense reference.

evidence.quote: we repeat the measurement on Qwen2.5-7B ( Qwen Team, 2024 ) over 5,000 5{,}000 AG News examples ( Zhang et al., 2015 ) with 20 % 20\% label noise, adapting the qkv projections of the last six blocks at twelve ranks up to d = 3584 d{=}3584 against dense fine-tuning of the same modules ( 3 3 shared seeds; Appendix C.3 ).
G G remains positive at every measured rank and in every seed, parity included.

papers.title: LoRA's Second Descent Extends Beyond Parameter Parity

papers.summary: ORCA applies soft orthogonality regularization early, then removes it. The paper reports lower final validation loss than Muon across LLaMA, Qwen3, and MoE settings, and a matched-target LLaMA run using 40% fewer tokens.
papers.relevance: Tests how the timing of spectral control affects effective rank and pretraining quality across scales.

evidence.quote: Across LLaMA, Qwen3, and fine-grained mixture-of-experts models ranging from 130M to 8B parameters, ORCA achieves lower final validation loss than Muon.
Therefore, ORCA used 40% fewer tokens to reach this target, a 1.66× token-efficiency gain.

papers.title: ORCA: The Annealed Spectral Conditioning Optimizer for Faster, Better LLM Training

papers.summary: BMuon changes Muon's spectral geometry to allocate a shared MLP-channel budget. On ViT-S/16 ImageNet-1K, it reports 74.08% Top-1 accuracy after 70% pruning without recovery, versus 74.17% before pruning.
papers.relevance: Directly probes whether optimizer geometry makes a trained model more compressible, though the highlighted result concerns structured pruning of a vision model rather than low-rank LLM compression.

evidence.quote: BMuon (BMuon) algorithm retains 74.08 % 74.08\% Top-1 accuracy after 70 % 70\% pruning, nearly matching its 74.17 % 74.17\% accuracy before pruning, with no post-pruning recovery.
The only persistent additional optimizer state is the allocation vector μ ∈ ℝ N \mu\in\mathbb{R}^{N} , one scalar per budgeted channel, which is negligible next to the momentum buffers.

papers.title: BMuon: Budgeting Muon's Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility

papers.summary: Idea2Prior builds an auditable idea-to-paper retrieval pipeline with identity checks, abstract assessment, citation expansion, and joint ranking. Its historical 30-query comparison reports Hit@5 of 16/30, versus 13/30 for ChatGPT web Deep Research and 11/30 for Gemini web Deep Research.
papers.relevance: Offers concrete retrieval, ranking, and auditability design choices for a research-digest agent.

evidence.quote: it preserves search queries, candidate identities, assessments, filtering reasons, PDF availability, and the final ranking.
The small, overlapping target set and historical protocol do not support a broad or statistically established superiority claim.

papers.title: Idea2Prior: Auditable Paper Retrieval and Ranking from Research Ideas

papers.summary: CORE is a training-free research-agent harness that retrieves passages but returns concise snippets, with expansion and deduplication controls. In closed-search comparisons, it reports higher answer accuracy and evidence recall across three agent models and three benchmarks.
papers.relevance: Directly informs retrieval and context-management choices in a handwritten digest harness.

evidence.quote: CORE’s context manager lets the agent expand the context around previously retrieved sources and deduplicates snippets across searches.
Across three agent models, CORE achieves the highest accuracy and evidence recall in every model–benchmark comparison, setting new state-of-the-art results to the best of our knowledge.

papers.title: CORE: Coarse-to-Fine Search with Context Management for Deep Research

papers.summary: A balanced, aligned matrix-factorization model derives how GD, SignGD, Muon, Shampoo, and K-FAC affect the birth and decay of singular modes. Its experiments show different transient rank trajectories despite comparable final loss and effective rank.
papers.relevance: Provides a mechanistic framework for optimizer-induced spectra and effective rank, with assumptions that limit direct transfer to LLMs.

evidence.quote: Under explicit balance and alignment assumptions, we derive birth, saturation, and decay laws for Euclidean GD, coordinate-wise updates of SignGD and an instantaneous Adam approximation, spectral updates of Muon and cumulative Shampoo, and a block curvature model of K-FAC.
Although the methods eventually reach similar losses and effective ranks, their trajectories differ substantially.

papers.title: Optimizer Geometry Sets the Pace: Spectral Learning Dynamics in Matrix Factorization

papers.summary: Spectrally Targeted Muon selectively orthogonalizes singular directions using Newton–Schulz-based projections. Its NanoGPT diagnostics report that targeted variants change update and parameter effective rank, but preserving Muon-like weight rank does not by itself match Muon's loss.
papers.relevance: Closely matches the question of how spectral optimizer updates affect weight spectra and model quality.

evidence.quote: tracking the effective rank of gradient, update, and weight matrices
AdamW collapses rank and still performs well, the bottom targeted variants keep Muon’s rank without matching its loss, and full-spectrum updates keep the spectrum flat for free.

papers.title: Spectrally Targeted Muon

papers.summary: Rotated Manifold Optimization respects the gauge symmetry of fixed-rank LoRA updates. In rank-16 Qwen2.5-3B RL fine-tuning, it reports higher accuracy than Adam on MATH-500, GSM8K, and OlympiadBench across three runs, at 1.08× per-step time.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses optimization of frozen-backbone low-rank factors and practical language-model fine-tuning.

evidence.quote: We design our optimizer on the manifold of fixed-rank matrices, aiming to optimize the product of the low-rank factors directly rather than each factor separately.

Unlike in SFT, where downstream differences among optimizers are relatively small, RoM shows a clearer advantage over Adam in RL finetuning, while requiring only 1.08 × 1.08\times the per-step training time on 4 NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs.

papers.title: Rotated Manifold Optimization for Low-Rank Adaptation

limitations: The Ori memory numbers measure additional peak memory during optimizer.step(), not total peak training memory.
BMuon's highlighted compression result is structured MLP-channel pruning on ViT-S/16, not low-rank compression of LLM weights.
CORE's reported comparisons use closed-search benchmarks, not a paper-digest evaluation.
Idea2Prior's historical comparison includes a convention-based ChatGPT hit and does not establish contamination-free or statistically general superiority.
The retrieved RoM passages do not quantify supervised fine-tuning gains or peak memory; its reported RL time cost should not be generalized to other settings.
